title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed networking progress (VPC peering, VPN, private endpoints), routing/NAT issues, recent kernel and runtime upgrade schedule, and performance results from last week's load test. Agreed on two network fixes, SE to rerun targeted perf tests, and security to validate KMS/HSM integration. Next meeting scheduled for 2026-07-29.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Aperture Head of MLOps), Maya Patel (Infra), Carlos Ruiz (Security), Samir Khan (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's routing fix, still seeing egress NAT flaps in staging, kernel upgrade scheduled for next Tuesday, plan to re-run perf tests after NAT change.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick check-in, we have about 40 minutes. how are we on the NAT change in staging, Maya?
[00:28] Maya Patel: yeah, hi. so we applied the route update last night, but we still saw, um, two sessions where egress IP rotated. looks like the autoscale spun up new nodes and they came with different egress. we think it's the private subnet using multiple nat gateways.
[01:05] Priya Rao: okay that matches what we saw; the pilot load tests show some token-level p95 variance when the egress changes, probably because the private endpoints were briefly failing over to the public path and then back. not a Redwood runtime issue per se but network-induced latency.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: just to be clear, this is in staging only, right? nothing in prod.
[01:48] Samir Khan: correct, staging only. but we can reproduce it with the ramp script that you shared, Alex.
[02:10] Alex Kim: good, thanks. so two parts: networking fix and then re-run the perf tests with the pinned model and quant profile. Priya, can you outline the perf test we'll run?
[02:38] Priya Rao: sure. last run was model v1.3 with int8 quantization, batch size 8 for generation path and batching turned on. we saw average throughput ~220 tokens/sec and p95 per-request latency ~620ms for a 256 token prompt under the stress test. when the egress flipped we saw spikes to 1.2s. we want to re-run with fixed egress and also test a smaller batch size (4) to evaluate latency tradeoffs.
[03:20] Carlos Ruiz: quick security question: with the cloud NAT change, do we need to update our KMS whitelist? our policy requires that any egress to the KMS endpoint be from the approved IP set.
[03:36] Alex Kim: yes, we flagged that last week. Redwood Private uses your KMS/HSM via a customer-managed endpoint — we need the CIDR list and the specific egress IPs. Maya, can you provide the updated egress IPs after the NAT change?
[03:55] Maya Patel: I can. once the NAT change is in staging and stable I'll dump the IP list and send it.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: also, are there any compatibility risks with the upcoming runtime kernel upgrade? we have a strict change freeze windows.
[04:22] Priya Rao: good call. the runtime upgrade is mostly a kernel patch for CUDA libs and some kernel-level scheduling improvements; we did internal smoke tests but we plan a canary in the pilot cluster first. rollback is straightforward — we keep the previous image and have automatic fallback if the health probe fails.
[04:50] Alex Kim: timeline is Tuesday night PST for the canary, full roll forward Thursday if canary is green. we will notify you 24 hours ahead.
[05:05] Samir Khan: can we get the exact image tags and the health probe criteria?
[05:12] Priya Rao: yes, I'll post the image tag and a short doc with probe thresholds to the pilot spreadsheet after this call.
[05:25] Alex Kim: perfect.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: going back to the networking, Samir pointed out earlier that we might benefit from a private endpoint rather than service endpoint for the Redwood control plane. any thoughts?
[05:45] Priya Rao: private endpoints reduce the cross-VPC hops, fewer NAT translations. the tradeoff is you need to set up interface endpoints and ensure DNS resolves correctly in your VPC. in our experience private endpoints lower p95 variance significantly for small bursts.
[06:10] Maya Patel: we tried an interface endpoint in another project and DNS split-horizon caused a weird redirect for internal test harness. it was fixable but took a few hours.
[06:28] Alex Kim: noted. we can provide a checklist for private endpoints to avoid common DNS pitfalls.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: on the perf front, Priya mentioned p95 of 620ms — is that for chat or single-turn generation?
[06:48] Priya Rao: that's single-turn generation with a 256 token prompt and 32 token generation. chat multi-turn runs slightly higher because we warm the KV cache but also have more KV IO. interestingly, when kv cache is warmed the p50 drops but p95 stays similar unless there's network wobble.
[07:15] Samir Khan: do you have a rough cost delta between batch size 8 and 4 in your config? we're trying to map cost vs latency.
[07:24] Priya Rao: ballpark: batch 8 is about 15-20% cheaper per token but can add 80-120ms to median latency. for Aperture's SLOs I think batch 4 might be a sweet spot unless you need max throughput.
[07:40] Jordan Lee: our production SLO is 500ms p95, so we're slightly over that in staging. we want to get under 500ms after these fixes.
[07:52] Alex Kim: understood. action plan: fix NAT egress -> re-run perf with batch 4 and pinned model -> if under 500ms p95 we move to ramp.
[08:10] Maya Patel: I will schedule the NAT rule change in staging tonight, ideally low traffic window.
[08:18] Carlos Ruiz: security item: we need the audit log formats for Redwood Private — do you ship object-level logs or event-level? also retention policy.
[08:30] Alex Kim: we provide audit logs at event-level with tokenized identifiers; retention can be configured — default is 90 days but enterprise plan supports longer retention. we will share the audit log schema doc.
[08:44] Carlos Ruiz: and SSO? we need SAML metadata for IdP integration for Redwoods console.
[08:50] Alex Kim: yes, SAML metadata and SSO guide will be attached to the checklist.
[09:00] Jordan Lee: great. anything else on security?
[09:05] Carlos Ruiz: just KMS HSM support — are you using external HSM or cloud-managed?
[09:12] Priya Rao: Redwood Private supports both; most customers in pilot use cloud KMS with their own keys. HSM integrations are available for the private/on-prem package; we'll ensure the integration notes are up in the shared folder.
[09:30] Samir Khan: quick question on model versioning — if we pin v1.3 and the runtime gets updated, does that impact the model artifacts?
[09:39] Priya Rao: model artifacts are separated from the runtime; pinning a model version ensures the same weights and tokenizer. runtime updates change execution kernels and may impact performance but not model semantics. we test compatibility during canary.
[09:58] Jordan Lee: can you remind us of fallback behavior if the private nodes get overloaded?
[10:05] Alex Kim: automatic fallback policy can route requests to a lower-cost hosted model variant if configured; for pilot we have fallback disabled by default but we can enable a limited fallback to a smaller model to keep latency low for critical paths.
[10:25] Maya Patel: for regulatory reasons we'd prefer no fallback off-site.
[10:30] Alex Kim: understood, we can keep everything within the VPC and only fallback to on-prem/dedicated within your account.
[10:38] Priya Rao: quick note on KV cache — warming helps with multi-turns but if the workload is highly diverse the cache hit rate is low; we recommend a hybrid approach with a short-lived prefix cache for important contexts.
[10:55] Jordan Lee: that makes sense. can we instrument cache hit rate in the dashboard?
[11:00] Alex Kim: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cache hit metrics per route; Priya will enable a pilot dashboard view for Aperture.
[11:12] Priya Rao: I'll add the dashboard link to the doc.
[11:18] Alex Kim: okay, next topic: kernel/runtime upgrade schedule and rollback. Priya?
[11:25] Priya Rao: canary Tuesday night, probe thresholds: 95% of requests < 700ms p95 for the canary baseline, health check must be green for 30 minutes. rollback will be triggered if error rates exceed 1% or p95 doubles. we also have an automated snapshot of KV cache state pre-upgrade so we can restore faster.
[11:52] Jordan Lee: any risk to data residency during the upgrade?
[11:58] Priya Rao: no, the control plane will not move data outside the VPC for Redwood Private; audit logs show the upgrade steps.
[12:08] Carlos Ruiz: please include the audit steps and the expected down window (if any).
[12:14] Priya Rao: down window should be negligible; canary may see small throttling for a few seconds during image swap but no data movement.
[12:28] Samir Khan: we will block major prod changes until after the pilot canary is green.
[12:35] Alex Kim: understood.
[12:40] Jordan Lee: can we talk briefly about tuning? the prompt set we shared — any obvious wins?
[12:46] Priya Rao: yes, a few: shorter context windows where not needed, static prompt templates for repetitive tasks to increase cache effectiveness, and token-regularization to limit over-generation. we can share tuned prompt examples.
[13:05] Maya Patel: when you say static templates, are you suggesting we persist parts of the prompt as part of state to get better KV hits?
[13:14] Priya Rao: exactly. instead of sending a 600 token prompt every time, persist the static portion in cache and only send dynamic parts — that reduces token compute and increases cache hit ratio.
[13:30] Jordan Lee: sounds good. any impact on throughput?
[13:34] Priya Rao: yes throughput improves because fewer tokens per call -> higher effective tokens/sec and lower latency.
[13:42] Alex Kim: action item for Priya to provide prompt templates and a sample integration snippet.
[13:48] Priya Rao: will do.
[13:52] Jordan Lee: also, on the procurement side, finance wants a rough TCO for the pilot at current config vs optimized config.
[14:03] Alex Kim: we can produce a TCO delta sheet; it'll include token cost, reserved capacity estimate, and expected savings from quantization and batching.
[14:15] Jordan Lee: good. please share before next meeting.
[14:20] Alex Kim: noted. Priya, anything else from SE side?
[14:25] Priya Rao: one thing — we noticed slightly higher memory pressure on the nodes during the stress run; we want to test a slightly higher memory instance in staging just to measure headroom. it doesn't mean we will change prod, but just to measure.
[14:42] Samir Khan: we can spin up a test node type for a couple hours tomorrow if needed.
[14:48] Priya Rao: that would help.
[14:52] Jordan Lee: timeline check: NAT fix tonight, perf re-run by Sunday, canary Tuesday, report Wednesday, ramp if green next week?
[15:07] Alex Kim: yes that sequence looks right.
[15:12] Maya Patel: can you note the exact tests you want? we have the ramp script but want the exact call pattern.
[15:20] Priya Rao: I will paste the exact ramp script parameters to the spreadsheet — 256 token prompts, QPS ramp 10->200 over 10 minutes, batch config X, seed set for determinism.
[15:34] Jordan Lee: great.
[15:38] Carlos Ruiz: security question about logs again: do you support central log shipping to our SIEM over private link or do you expect logs to be pulled?
[15:48] Alex Kim: we support push to S3 or direct syslog over a private endpoint. we can set up a forwarder in the VPC to your SIEM if you prefer push.
[16:00] Carlos Ruiz: prefer push.
[16:04] Alex Kim: will include config details in the checklist.
[16:10] Priya Rao: quick gotcha — when you enable push, make sure to limit permissions to the log bucket to the logging role and enable SSE with your KMS.
[16:22] Carlos Ruiz: yes we will.
[16:26] Jordan Lee: anything else?
[16:30] Alex Kim: a couple small notes from last week's test: the quantized model showed a 12% throughput improvement on the same hardware and CPU utilization dropped slightly; memory footprints were similar. We also saw a small regression in one eval case, we created a bug for it so SE will dig in.
[16:54] Priya Rao: right, the regression is in hallucination for a rare prompt — we'll add that to the evals sheet and run a targeted comparison.
[17:06] Jordan Lee: okay, thanks. can we summarize decisions?
[17:10] Alex Kim: decisions: 1) proceed with NAT rule change in staging tonight, 2) SE will rerun perf tests with batch 4 and pinned v1.3, 3) canary runtime upgrade Tuesday night, 4) no offsite fallback without explicit signoff, 5) provide KMS whitelist IPs and audit schema.
[17:36] Maya Patel: agreed.
[17:40] Carlos Ruiz: agreed.
[17:44] Alex Kim: I'll follow up with the updated network diagram and the security checklist. Priya will post the ramp script and image tags.
[17:56] Priya Rao: I'll also enable a pilot dashboard view and upload the perf baseline CSV.
[18:04] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. next sync same time next week?
[18:09] Alex Kim: yep, 2026-07-29 10:00 AM UTC. I'll send the invite.
[18:16] Samir Khan: thanks all.
[18:20] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains some ASR artifacts (Redwood Privet, KV cash, etc.) intentionally left to reflect real transcription. Links referenced: pilot spreadsheet (link shared in chat), security checklist (to be attached), perf CSV (to be uploaded).
questions: Will the NAT change affect prod? - No, staging only
What are the rollback criteria for the kernel upgrade? - error rate >1% or p95 doubles
Can Redwood push logs to customer SIEM? - yes via private endpoint/push
